metadata.title: Complex Financial Reasoning Evaluation Questions
metadata.description: Non-trivial questions requiring multi-step analysis, optimization, and personalized recommendations

questions.question: I earn 45,000 NOK per month and currently spend 15,000 on housing, 8,000 on food, 6,000 on transport, and 3,000 on entertainment. I want to save 10,000 NOK per month to buy a house. What specific changes should I make to my budget?
expected_reasoning_steps: Calculate current total expenses and savings
Identify gap between current and desired savings
Get Norwegian average spending for comparison
Optimize budget allocation using advanced tools
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires multi-factor optimization, trade-off analysis, and specific actionable recommendations based on Norwegian norms

questions.question: I earn 55,000 NOK per month. My expenses are: housing 18,000, food 7,000, transport 5,000, entertainment 3,000, other 4,000. Am I financially healthy? What are my biggest risks?
expected_reasoning_steps: Analyze budget health using multi-factor scoring
Detect spending anomalies vs Norwegian averages
Calculate savings rate and compare to recommendations
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires comprehensive health assessment, statistical anomaly detection, and risk prioritization

questions.question: I want to live in Oslo with housing costs of 20,000 NOK/month, spend 10,000 on food and dining, 7,000 on transport (own a car), 5,000 on entertainment, and save 20% of my income. What salary do I need?
expected_reasoning_steps: Calculate required income for 20% savings rate
Compare desired lifestyle to Norwegian averages
Assess affordability at different income levels
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires reverse calculation, lifestyle assessment, and feasibility analysis

questions.question: I want to buy a 300,000 NOK car. I earn 50,000 NOK per month, have 100,000 NOK saved, and my monthly expenses are 35,000 NOK. Should I buy it now, finance it, or save longer?
expected_reasoning_steps: Calculate time to save for full purchase
Compare options and recommend best approach
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires multi-period analysis, financing calculations, and risk-benefit assessment

questions.question: I earn 60,000 NOK per month and spend 16,000 on housing, 9,000 on food, 7,000 on transport, 5,000 on entertainment, and 4,000 on other expenses. How much could I realistically save per month if I optimize my budget?
expected_reasoning_steps: Identify optimization opportunities in each category
Calculate savings potential with difficulty levels
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires opportunity analysis, prioritization, and phased implementation planning

questions.question: My family of 4 earns 80,000 NOK per month. We spend 25,000 on housing, 12,000 on food, 8,000 on transport, 6,000 on entertainment, and 5,000 on other expenses. We want to save for our children's education. What's the maximum we can save monthly while maintaining a comfortable lifestyle?
expected_reasoning_steps: Balance family needs with savings goals
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires family-specific considerations, multi-objective optimization, and long-term planning

questions.question: I spend 22,000 NOK per month on housing (50% of my 44,000 NOK income), 6,000 on food, 4,000 on transport, and 2,000 on entertainment. What are the red flags in my budget?
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires anomaly detection, risk assessment, and prioritized interventions

questions.question: Can I afford to move from Trondheim to Oslo if it increases my housing from 12,000 to 20,000 NOK per month? I earn 55,000 NOK and currently save 15,000 per month.
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires scenario comparison, impact analysis, and decision support

questions.question: I'm considering buying a 3.5 million NOK apartment in Bergen. I earn 70,000 NOK per month, have 500,000 saved, and spend 45,000 per month. Is this affordable? What down payment and loan terms should I aim for?
expected_reasoning_steps: Calculate required down payment (15% for house)
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires mortgage calculations, affordability assessment, and long-term financial planning

questions.question: I want to save 500,000 NOK in 3 years for a down payment on a house. I earn 50,000 per month and currently save 8,000 per month. How can I reach my goal?
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires goal-based planning, gap analysis, and actionable strategy

questions.question: I'm a student earning 25,000 NOK per month (part-time + student loan). I spend 10,000 on housing, 4,000 on food, 2,000 on transport, 3,000 on entertainment, and 2,000 on other expenses. How can I improve my financial situation?
expected_reasoning_steps: Analyze budget health for low income
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires context-aware analysis for low-income scenario with limited optimization options

questions.question: Compare my spending to Norwegian averages and tell me if I'm overspending anywhere: Income 48,000 NOK, housing 14,000, food 9,000, transport 8,000, entertainment 6,000, other 3,000.
expected_reasoning_steps: Get Norwegian averages for all categories
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires comprehensive comparative analysis and statistical interpretation

questions.question: I want to work part-time (30,000 NOK/month) to have better work-life balance. Currently I earn 50,000 and spend 38,000 per month. Is this lifestyle change financially viable?
expected_reasoning_steps: Calculate new income vs current expenses
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires income reduction scenario analysis and lifestyle trade-off evaluation

questions.question: Should I buy a 150,000 NOK used car or lease a new car for 4,000 NOK per month? I earn 45,000 NOK, have 80,000 saved, and spend 32,000 per month.
expected_reasoning_steps: Assess impact on budget for both options
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires multi-option comparison and total cost of ownership analysis

questions.question: I'm 30 years old and want to retire at 60 with 10 million NOK saved. I currently earn 60,000 per month and save 12,000. Am I on track? What should I do?
expected_reasoning_steps: Compare current vs required savings rate
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires long-term financial planning and retirement goal assessment

questions.question: I just got a 10,000 NOK raise (now earning 55,000 per month). How should I allocate this extra money between savings, lifestyle improvements, and debt repayment? I currently save 8,000 per month.
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires multi-objective optimization and financial priority assessment

questions.question: I'm spending 3,000 NOK per month on entertainment (income 40,000 NOK). Is this too much? What's reasonable?
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires contextual analysis and norm-based recommendations

questions.question: I'm considering having a child. My partner and I earn 90,000 NOK combined and spend 60,000 per month. Can we afford childcare costs of 5,000 NOK per month while maintaining our current lifestyle?
expected_reasoning_steps: Evaluate financial health with new expense
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires life event planning and family budget analysis

questions.question: I want to pursue a master's degree costing 200,000 NOK total. I earn 45,000 per month and have 50,000 saved. Should I take a student loan, save up, or work part-time during studies?
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires education investment analysis and multi-option comparison

questions.question: I have 100,000 NOK in emergency savings. Is this enough? I earn 50,000 per month and spend 38,000. Should I save more or invest the excess?
expected_reasoning_steps: Calculate recommended emergency fund (3-6 months expenses)
questions.why_nontrivial: Requires emergency fund assessment and financial planning guidance
